templates.title: Watchtower
templates.description: Automatically update running Docker containers to the latest image version.

env.name: TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Timezone for the container (e.g. Europe/Madrid)

env.name: WATCHTOWER_CLEANUP
env.label: Remove old images
env.description: Remove old images after updating containers

env.name: WATCHTOWER_POLL_INTERVAL
env.label: Poll interval (seconds)
env.description: Interval in seconds between checks for updates

env.name: WATCHTOWER_INCLUDE_STOPPED
env.label: Include stopped containers
env.description: Also check stopped containers for updates

env.name: WATCHTOWER_REVIVE_STOPPED
env.label: Revive stopped containers
env.description: Start stopped containers after updating their image

templates.note: Watchtower monitors running containers and automatically updates them when a new image version is available. It requires access to the Docker socket.

templates.title: UniFi Controller
templates.description: Ubiquiti UniFi Network Management Controller for managing UniFi devices.

env.name: TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Timezone for the container (e.g. Europe/Madrid)

env.name: PUID
env.label: User ID (PUID)
env.description: User ID that the container process will run as

env.name: PGID
env.label: Group ID (PGID)
env.description: Group ID that the container process will run as

env.name: MONGO_USER
env.label: MongoDB username
env.description: Username for the MongoDB database

templates.title: Prometheus & Loki
templates.description: Full monitoring stack: Prometheus for metrics, Loki for log aggregation, Promtail for log shipping, and Grafana for visualization.

env.name: PROMETHEUS_RETENTION
env.label: Prometheus retention period
env.description: How long Prometheus keeps metrics data (e.g. 15d, 30d)

env.name: GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER
env.label: Grafana admin username
env.description: Username for the Grafana admin account

env.name: GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.label: Grafana admin password
env.description: Password for the Grafana admin account

templates.note:
• Prometheus: http://localhost:9090
  • Loki: http://localhost:3100
  • Grafana: http://localhost:3000 — add Prometheus (http://prometheus:9090) and Loki (http://loki:3100) as data sources.

templates.title: Plex Media Server
templates.description: Plex Media Server: stream your media library to any device. Uses the qnet network with a fixed MAC address.

env.name: TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Timezone for the container (e.g. Europe/Madrid)

env.name: PUID
env.label: User ID (PUID)
env.description: User ID that Plex will run as

env.name: PGID
env.label: Group ID (PGID)
env.description: Group ID that Plex will run as

env.name: PLEX_CLAIM
env.label: Plex Claim Token
env.description: Get your claim token from https://plex.tv/claim (required on first run)

env.name: ADVERTISE_IP
env.label: Advertise IP
env.description: IP advertised for remote access (e.g. http://192.168.1.100:32400)

env.name: PLEX_CONFIG_PATH
env.label: Plex config path
env.description: Path where Plex configuration will be stored on the NAS

env.name: MEDIA_PATH
env.label: Media path
env.description: Path to your media folder on the NAS

templates.note:
Plex Media Server web interface at http://localhost:32400/web.

This stack uses the qnet-static-bond0-0094fd network with a fixed MAC address (02:00:00:00:00:01) so Plex does not generate a new identity on each restart.

First run: Get a claim token at https://plex.tv/claim and set it in the environment variable PLEX_CLAIM.

Hardware transcoding via /dev/dri is enabled if available on your NAS (Intel Quick Sync).

To add more media paths, go to Volumes in the advanced deployment view and add additional bind mounts.
